title: Run with Jordan
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). After a run, Alex and Jordan talk half-marathon training, Alex's knee pain and strength work, and sleep and recovery, with a quick joke aside and Jordan promising to send a training plan.

utterances.text: Okay, that last kilometer was rough. You good?
Yeah, just dying a little. What was that, eight k?
Eight point four. You're way faster than a month ago, though.
Thanks. I'm trying to get serious about the half marathon. It's ten weeks out and I don't really have a plan. I just run whenever I feel like it.
That's the problem. You need one long run a week, a couple of easy ones, and maybe one faster session. And most of it should feel slow.
Slow? Like conversation slow?
Like this conversation, yeah. People run their easy days too hard and then they're cooked for the long run.
Okay, that's definitely me. Every run is just me trying not to get passed.
Speaking of getting passed, did you see that kid on the scooter by the bridge?
The one with the helmet with ears on it? He looked right at me and sped up. I've never felt so judged by a five-year-old.
Ha! He had better form than you, too.
Rude. True, but rude. Anyway, the bigger issue is my knee. The outside of my right knee gets this sharp thing after like six k.
Outside of the knee? That's usually not the knee itself. It's often weak hips and glutes, so the knee takes the hit.
Wait, really? So my butt is the problem?
Kind of, yeah. I had the exact same thing two years ago. What fixed it was strength work, twice a week. Glute bridges, side planks, step-downs off a box, single-leg squats.
I've never done any strength stuff. I just run.
Most runners don't. But even twenty minutes after an easy run helps. And go slower on the step-downs than feels necessary. That's where the control comes from.
Should I stop running until it's better?
I'm not a physio, so if it gets worse, go see one. But for me, cutting the long run back a bit and doing the strength work was enough.
Okay. How are you even recovering from all this, though? You run like five times a week.
Honestly? Sleep. That's the boring secret. If I get under seven hours, my legs feel like concrete the next day.
Yeah, I've been sleeping terribly. Work stuff. I keep waking up at four.
That'll wreck your training more than any knee. Your body does the actual adapting while you sleep. The run is just the stress.
So the run doesn't make me fitter, the recovery does?
Basically. Run, eat, sleep. And take the rest days seriously. They're not lazy days, they're part of the plan.
I like that framing. Rest days are training.
Okay, look, I'll send you my plan tonight. It's the one I used last spring. Ten weeks, with the strength days built in.
That would be amazing. Seriously.
I'll put notes on which runs should feel easy so you stop racing children on scooters.
No promises. Same time Saturday for the long one?
Saturday, nine a.m. Bring water this time.
